claim_boundary.execution_health: A passing execution contract or canary establishes only that the configured adapter ran and produced validated output over disclosed targets.
claim_boundary.detection_capability: Capabilities describe implemented rule or advisory coverage; they do not establish exhaustive recall, exploitability, actionability, or project-wide precision.
claim_boundary.candidate_policy: Every match remains an unadjudicated review candidate until repository evidence supports a disposition.

status_semantics.complete: Applicable execution with validated output, at least one disclosed target, and at least one candidate.
status_semantics.empty: Applicable execution with validated output, at least one disclosed target, and zero candidates; not proof that the repository is vulnerability-free.
status_semantics.not-applicable: The adapter found zero inputs it can evaluate under its production applicability policy and retains an explicit applicability_detail.
status_semantics.partial: Validated results cover only a disclosed subset or fallback mode; failure_detail states the missing coverage.
status_semantics.unavailable: The scanner binary or required executable capability was unavailable, so no coverage claim is made.
status_semantics.failed: Execution, target verification, or output validation failed with attributable detail; no clean-zero claim is permitted.
status_semantics.disabled: Deterministic tools were explicitly disabled; no coverage claim is made.

mechanisms: Rule-defined source-code security patterns and data flows
Rule-defined framework, configuration, CI, infrastructure, and secret patterns in the pinned official pack
ecosystems: Languages and technologies represented by the 1,073-rule pinned official default pack
scanners.applicability: Applicable when the verified pinned configuration selects at least one non-symlink file; zero selected targets is failed, not empty.
inputs: Repository source and configuration files selected by Semgrep
scanners.configuration: Vendored p/default payload verified by decompressed SHA-256 before execution; 1,073 rules in the 2026-07-29 snapshot.
strengths: Exact file/line candidates from validated normalized SARIF
Verified target report distinguishes a clean scan from an unexplained zero
blind_spots: Public rules miss nonstandard and advisory-specific mechanisms even when execution is healthy
Matches do not establish attacker control, reachability, mitigation, or actionability
No exhaustive cross-service or business-logic analysis
scanners.canary: Local Python shell-invocation rule with a safe argument-vector negative control.

mechanisms: Variable or concatenated JavaScript/TypeScript commands passed to child_process.exec or execSync
scanners.applicability: Applicable only when a non-symlink .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, or .tsx file exists.
scanners.configuration: Separately invoked packaged one-rule YAML with its own SHA-256, rule count, SARIF, target report, status, and producer identity.
strengths: Qualified vulnerable-only recovery for the frozen codecov-node target
Manufactured positive and argument-vector negative controls exercise the production rule
blind_spots: Only one qualified mechanism and two languages are in scope
A shell sink match is not proof of attacker control or command injection
SQL construction, SSRF, archive extraction, and traversal await separate qualification
scanners.canary: Variable execSync positive and execFileSync argument-vector negative using the packaged rule.

mechanisms: Known PyPI package-version advisories for dependencies declared in submitted requirements files
scanners.applicability: Applicable only when at least one root-level requirements*.txt file is present.
scanners.configuration: Pinned binary plus the live PyPI Advisory Database; query time is retained and database version remains null when unavailable.
strengths: Reports affected package, version, advisory, and fixes
Exact direct pins can use a disclosed no-transitive-resolution partial fallback
blind_spots: The production adapter does not submit poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, pdm.lock, pyproject.toml, or nested requirements files to pip-audit
An advisory match does not establish vulnerable-code use or exploitability
Live advisory responses can change between identical binary/manifest runs
scanners.canary: Known vulnerable exact Python pin and an applicable empty requirements file.

mechanisms: Known OSV advisories for packages and versions resolved from supported package sources
ecosystems: Package ecosystems and source/lockfile formats supported by the pinned OSV-Scanner binary
scanners.applicability: Recursively discovers supported package sources. After a no-source result, up to 100 discovered requirements*.txt files are tried explicitly; no supported source is not-applicable.
inputs: Bounded explicit requirements*.txt fallback after recursive no-source failure
scanners.configuration: Pinned binary plus live OSV.dev; query time is retained and database version remains null when unavailable.
strengths: No-source behavior is distinct from a validated clean scan
blind_spots: Coverage is limited to formats recognized by the pinned binary
The requirements fallback is partial and does not recover other missed manifest types
Advisory matches do not establish reachability or exploitability
scanners.canary: Known vulnerable package source and a root with no supported manifest, expected not-applicable.

mechanisms: Rule-defined credential, token, key, and secret-like patterns in snapshot content
scanners.applicability: Applicable to every submitted snapshot root when the binary is available.
inputs: Repository snapshot scanned without Git history
scanners.configuration: Rules embedded in the pinned gitleaks binary; binary version and embedded-default identity are retained.
strengths: Matched secret values are redacted before persistence
Validated empty JSON distinguishes clean execution from failure
blind_spots: --no-git means repository history is not inspected
Matches can be placeholders, examples, test values, or revoked credentials
No match does not establish safety of runtime or external secrets
scanners.canary: Synthetic Stripe-shaped credential and an environment-placeholder negative control.

scanners.applicability: Applicable when at least one non-test .java source file exists in the exact submitted snapshot.
inputs: Java source indexed from the submitted repository snapshot
scanners.configuration: Embedded weak_rng@v1 idiom set; index binding to the submitted snapshot is verified before detection.
strengths: Stable file, line, enclosing-symbol, and idiom identities
Skips comments, test sources, SecureRandom, and RandomStringUtils secure variants
blind_spots: A match does not prove security-sensitive use, attacker observation, state recovery, or exploitability
Aliases, wrappers, indirect data flow, and unimplemented generator idioms may be missed
scanners.canary: Java new Random positive and SecureRandom negative controls using the production adapter.
